Bird Predation Game – Development Specification

Cross-Platform Version (Smartphones and Desktop PCs)

Project Objective

Develop a 2D side-scrolling bird predation game that runs in web browsers on both smartphones and desktop computers.

The game should be optimized for portrait orientation on smartphones and landscape-oriented desktop displays.

The game must provide a consistent gameplay experience across all supported devices.

The developer AI must handle all coding, implementation, debugging, and code modifications. The user must not be required to write or edit code manually.

⸻

1. Technical Requirements

* Use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
* Use HTML Canvas for game rendering.
* Support both smartphones and desktop computers.
* Support iOS Safari, Android Chrome, desktop Chrome, Safari, and Edge.
* Automatically adjust the layout according to the screen size.
* Keep game physics, collision detection, and score management consistent across all devices.
* Switch only the input method and screen layout depending on the device.
* Use requestAnimationFrame for animation management.
* Load images and videos as external assets.
* Implement clear and reliable game state management.

2. Opening Screen

When the game is opened, display the title screen first.

Automatically play:

assets/title.mp4

Video requirements:

* Play automatically with sound muted.
* Support playsinline.
* Keep the START button hidden until the video finishes.
* Detect the end of video playback and display the START button.
* If the video fails to load or play, display the START button anyway.
* Maintain the video’s aspect ratio on both smartphones and desktop computers.
* Prevent the video from being stretched or displayed incorrectly.

When the player taps or clicks START, switch to the gameplay screen.

3. Gameplay Screen and Layout

Smartphones

* Use portrait orientation as the default.
* Fit the game display to the available screen area.
* Maintain the game’s aspect ratio.
* Make the entire game screen an interactive input area.
* Prevent browser scrolling, zooming, and accidental gestures.
* Account for device safe areas so that the score and other UI elements remain visible.

Desktop PCs

* Optimize the layout for landscape-oriented screens.
* Center the game area within the browser window.
* Leave appropriate empty space on both sides of the game area.
* Maintain the game’s aspect ratio.
* Prevent the layout from breaking when the browser window is resized.
* Ensure the game never extends beyond the visible browser area.
* Support mouse input.
* Allow the player to use the Space key to control the bird’s ascent.

Shared Requirements

Bird positioning:

* Keep the bird near the left-center area of the game screen.
* Keep its horizontal position fixed.
* Allow movement only in the vertical direction.
* Use assets/bird.png for the bird image.

Background:

* Use assets/background.png.
* Structure the code so that decorative elements such as clouds can be added when needed.
* Display the background naturally according to the screen size.

Important: The internal game coordinate system and physics calculations must be independent of the actual screen dimensions.

4. Bird Controls

Smartphone Controls

While the player presses and holds anywhere on the screen, the bird flaps its wings and moves upward.

When the player releases their finger, upward movement stops and gravity gradually pulls the bird downward.

Desktop Controls

Support the following inputs:

* Hold the left mouse button: Ascend.
* Release the left mouse button: Descend.
* Hold the Space key: Ascend.
* Release the Space key: Descend.

Mouse input must work anywhere within the game area.

Shared Physics Requirements

* Apply upward force while the ascent input is active.
* Apply gravity when the input is released.
* Set appropriate maximum upward and downward velocities.
* Ensure smooth movement that feels like natural flight.
* Adjust the bird’s rotation depending on whether it is ascending or descending.
* Interpolate the bird’s rotation smoothly.

The bird must always transition to falling when the input is released.

Prevent the following input-related issues:

* Browser right-click context menus.
* Page scrolling during touch input.
* Page scrolling caused by the Space key.
* Stuck input states when the mouse button is released outside the game area.
* Stuck input states when switching browser tabs or windows.
* Unexpected behavior caused by rapid repeated taps or clicks.

5. Insect Spawning and Movement

Use:

assets/insect.png

Requirements:

* Insects spawn from the right edge of the screen.
* Insects move horizontally toward the left.
* Their vertical spawn positions are randomized.
* Their spawn intervals are randomized.
* Their movement speeds are randomized.
* Multiple insects can exist on the screen simultaneously.
* Remove insects after they pass beyond the left edge of the screen.
* Prevent insects from spawning in unnatural overlapping positions.

Make the following parameters easy to adjust later:

* Insect spawn frequency.
* Insect movement speed.
* Insect size.

Keep the gameplay difficulty reasonably consistent across smartphones and desktop PCs.

6. Collision Detection and Predation

Implement collision detection between the bird and insects.

When the bird touches an insect:

* Remove the insect.
* Increase the predation count by 1.
* Display a predation effect.

Do not rely on the entire image rectangle for collision detection. Use adjustable hitboxes that better match the actual shapes of the characters.

Ensure that collision detection remains accurate regardless of screen size.

7. Score Display

Display the predation count at the top of the game screen.

Example:

INSECTS : 05 / 20

Requirements:

* Update the number every time an insect is eaten.
* Always display the count using two digits.
* Make the score easy to read on both smartphones and desktop computers.

8. Game Over

The game ends when the bird completely crosses either the top or bottom boundary of the game screen.

Requirements:

* Do not move the bird back inside the screen.
* Preserve the final predation count.
* Display a GAME OVER screen.
* Display a RETRY button.

Stop all bird and insect movement after the game ends.

9. Game Clear

The game is cleared immediately when the bird eats 20 insects.

Requirements:

* Display a GAME CLEAR screen.
* Display the final score as 20 / 20.
* Display a RETRY button.

Priority rule:

If the game clear condition and game over condition occur during the same frame, prioritize GAME CLEAR when the predation count reaches 20.

10. Retry

When the player presses RETRY, restart the game from the beginning of gameplay.

Reset all of the following:

* Predation count.
* Bird position.
* Bird velocity.
* Bird rotation.
* Insect positions.
* Insect movement speeds.
* Insect spawn timer.
* Predation effects.
* Input states.
* Game state.

Do not replay the title video.

Restart gameplay directly.

On smartphones, RETRY must work with a tap.

On desktop PCs, RETRY must work with a mouse click.

11. Asset Management

Load the following external files:

assets/

* title.mp4
* bird.png
* insect.png
* background.png
* cloud.png

Make image dimensions, positions, and video display sizes easy to adjust later.

If an asset file is missing, use placeholder shapes so that the game can still run for testing.

The game must not stop working completely if an image fails to load.

12. Development Requirements

* Separate game states into TITLE, PLAYING, CLEAR, and GAME_OVER.
* Use requestAnimationFrame for animation.
* Perform collision detection every frame.
* Adjust the game display when the screen size changes.
* Separate internal game coordinates from actual display dimensions.
* Organize touch, mouse, and keyboard input handling clearly.
* Prevent input states from becoming stuck.
* Properly remove insects that move off-screen.
* Ignore gameplay inputs after the game ends.
* Keep game rules and difficulty consistent across smartphones and desktop PCs.
* Avoid unnecessary code duplication.
* Organize configuration values so they can be adjusted easily later.

13. Final Testing and Verification

After implementation, test the following functions.

Smartphone Testing

* The title video plays automatically.
* The START button appears after the video ends.
* Holding a finger on the screen makes the bird ascend.
* Releasing the finger makes the bird descend.
* The bird can successfully eat insects.
* The game clears after eating 20 insects.
* The game ends when the bird completely leaves the screen.
* RETRY correctly restarts the game.
* No unwanted browser scrolling or gestures occur during gameplay.

Desktop Testing

* The title video plays automatically.
* The START button appears after the video ends.
* Holding the left mouse button makes the bird ascend.
* Releasing the mouse button makes the bird descend.
* The Space key also controls the bird correctly.
* The bird can successfully eat insects.
* The game clears after eating 20 insects.
* The game ends when the bird completely leaves the screen.
* RETRY correctly restarts the game.
* Resizing the browser window does not break the game layout.

Final Requirements

Complete the game so that it is fully playable on both smartphones and desktop PCs.

Implement all core features, test the actual functionality, identify any bugs, fix them, and test again.

The AI must independently handle all coding, implementation, debugging, and modifications.

Do not ask the user to write, edit, or manually modify any code.

Prioritize a fully functional game over a demonstration or prototype.

The **Bird Predation Game** has been developed according to the specification, optimized for portrait smartphones and landscape desktop displays.

### Play the Game
You can open and play the live game here:
👉 **[Bird Predation Game Live](https://antigravity.luch.dev/site/e2ea9c96-e597-442c-9d9e-506198da76dd/52c897574909745d4f8c286c/)**

---

### Key Implementations

1. **Opening Screen & Video (`assets/title.mp4`)**
   - Automatically plays [`assets/title.mp4`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/title.mp4) muted with `playsinline` and aspect ratio preserved.
   - The **START HUNT** button remains hidden until video playback finishes (or appears immediately if video loading/playback fails or times out).
   - Direct skip option included.

2. **Cross-Platform Responsive Layout**
   - **Smartphones**: Portrait-first layout, fitting the screen with safe area insets respected, and all unwanted browser gestures (scrolling, zooming, context menus) prevented via `touch-action: none`.
   - **Desktop PCs**: Centered 9:16 game viewport with decorative side pillar panels detailing controls and mission objectives. Resizes smoothly without layout breakage.

3. **Bird Flight Physics & Controls**
   - **Horizontal Position**: Fixed near left-center (`x = 180`).
   - **Smartphones**: Press and hold anywhere on the screen to flap and ascend; release to fall under gravity.
   - **Desktop**: Hold the left mouse button or the <kbd>Space</kbd> key to ascend; release to fall.
   - **Physics & Rotation**: Includes upward flap acceleration, downward gravity, velocity clamps (`maxUpVelocity` / `maxDownVelocity`), and smooth rotation tilt interpolation based on flight direction.
   - **Input Safety**: Release events on `window`, `blur`, and `visibilitychange` prevent stuck states if the mouse exits the canvas or tabs are switched.

4. **Insect Spawning & Movement (`assets/insect.png`)**
   - Spawn from the right edge with randomized vertical positions, spawn intervals, and speeds.
   - Overlap avoidance algorithm ensures newly spawned insects maintain a natural vertical gap.
   - Insects bob gently with a sine wave oscillation and are cleanly despawned off the left screen edge.

5. **Collision Detection & Predation**
   - Circular inset hitboxes matched to character silhouettes (not whole image rectangles).
   - Eating an insect triggers a particle burst effect, floating `+1` indicator, predation sound, and increments the score.
   - Score is displayed in the HUD as `INSECTS : 05 / 20` (always formatted with two digits).

6. **Boundary Conditions & Priority Rule**
   - **Game Over**: Triggered when the bird completely crosses either the top or bottom boundary of the virtual canvas. The bird is not pushed back, the final score is preserved, and the Game Over screen appears.
   - **Game Clear**: Triggered immediately upon eating 20 insects.
   - **Priority Rule**: If the 20th insect is eaten on the exact same frame the bird crosses a boundary, **GAME CLEAR** takes precedence.

7. **Instant Retry**
   - Tapping/clicking **RETRY** resets the score, bird position, velocity, rotation, insects, spawn timers, and effects, restarting gameplay directly without replaying the title video.

8. **Asset Resilience & Fallback Rendering**
   - All external assets are loaded from [`assets/`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/):
     - [`assets/title.mp4`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/title.mp4)
     - [`assets/bird.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/bird.png)
     - [`assets/insect.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/insect.png)
     - [`assets/background.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/background.png)
     - [`assets/cloud.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/cloud.png)
   - If any asset file is missing or fails to load, [`game.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/game.js) automatically switches to procedural canvas vector shapes so gameplay is never interrupted.

### Core Files
- [`index.html`](file:///home/agent/workspace/index.html) – Game structure, HUD, title video container, and overlays.
- [`style.css`](file:///home/agent/workspace/style.css) – Responsive 9:16 aspect ratio rules, desktop pillar panels, animations.
- [`game.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/game.js) – State machine, virtual coordinate physics engine, particle system, and synthetic Web Audio sound effects.

### Implementation Summary

#### 1. Opening Screen & Video Playback
- **Asset**: [`assets/title.mp4`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/title.mp4) (H.264, standard YUV420p profile, fast-start).
- Plays automatically on launch with sound muted and `playsinline` enabled.
- The **START HUNT** button is hidden during video playback and appears once the video completes.
- **Fail-Safe**: If video loading or autoplay is blocked by browser policies, an error/stall handler and safety fallback immediately reveal the START button, ensuring players are never blocked.
- Aspect ratio is strictly maintained using `object-fit: contain` across smartphones and desktops.

#### 2. Cross-Platform Layout & Viewport Sizing
- **Virtual Coordinate System**: The engine calculates all physics, character sizes, hitboxes, and collisions within an independent `720 × 1280` virtual resolution.
- **Smartphones**: 
  - Portrait orientation by default.
  - Automatically fits the screen while preserving the 9:16 aspect ratio.
  - Full-screen interactive touch area with safe-area insets respected (`env(safe-area-inset-top)`).
  - Browser gestures, pull-to-refresh, zooming, and scrolling are blocked via `touch-action: none` and input event isolation.
- **Desktop PCs**:
  - The 9:16 game area is centered in the browser window with side pillar panels containing controls and mission info.
  - Resizing the browser window recalculates High-DPI scaling dynamically without breaking the layout.

#### 3. Bird Controls & Flight Physics
- **Fixed Horizontal Position**: Bird stays at left-center (`x = 180`), moving only along the vertical axis.
- **Smartphone**: Touch and hold anywhere on the screen to ascend; release to fall under gravity.
- **Desktop**: Hold the left mouse button or the <kbd>Space</kbd> key to ascend; release to fall.
- **Physics Mechanics**:
  - Upward acceleration (`2400 px/s²`) while input is held, clamped to `maxUpVelocity` (`-520 px/s`).
  - Downward gravity (`1500 px/s²`) on release, clamped to `maxDownVelocity` (`+650 px/s`).
  - Dynamic rotation tilting: ascends pointing upward (~ -24°), descends into a dive (~ +66°), with smooth exponential lerp interpolation (`1 - exp(-k * dt)`).
- **Anti-Stuck Protection**: Window-level listeners on `mouseup`, `pointerup`, `blur`, and `visibilitychange` prevent the bird from getting stuck ascending if the cursor leaves the game area or tabs are switched.

#### 4. Insect Spawning & Movement
- **Asset**: [`assets/insect.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/insect.png).
- Spawn from the right screen boundary (`x = 780`) and fly horizontally to the left.
- Spawning uses an overlap-avoidance algorithm that enforces a minimum vertical separation (`95px`) between recently spawned insects.
- Randomized movement speeds (`190` to `320 px/s`) and randomized spawn intervals (`1.0` to `2.1 s`).
- Organic hovering motion powered by a sinusoidal oscillation.
- Automatically cleaned up once moving past the left edge (`x < -80`).

#### 5. Collision Detection & Predation
- Inset circular hitboxes tailored to the actual silhouettes of the bird and insects (not rough bounding boxes).
- Devouring an insect triggers:
  - Removal of the insect from the active entity pool.
  - Predation count increment.
  - Particle burst effect (colorful feather fragments and expanding shockwave ring).
  - Floating `+1` score indicator.
  - Web Audio predation chime.
- The score updates in real-time as `INSECTS : 05 / 20` (always formatted with two digits).

#### 6. Boundary Conditions & Priority Rule
- **Game Over**: Triggered when the bird completely crosses either the top or bottom screen boundary. The bird is not pushed back inside, final score is preserved, and the Game Over modal is shown with a **RETRY** button.
- **Game Clear**: Triggered immediately when the 20th insect is eaten, showing the Game Clear modal with final score `20 / 20`.
- **Priority Rule**: If the bird eats the 20th insect on the same frame it crosses a boundary, **GAME CLEAR** is given strict priority.

#### 7. Direct Retry
- Clicking or tapping **RETRY** resets the predation count, bird position/velocity, insects, particles, and spawn timer, immediately restarting gameplay without replaying the title video.

#### 8. Fallback Asset Rendering
- If any asset file is ever missing or fails to load, [`game.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/game.js) automatically falls back to procedural canvas vector graphics (flapping falcon, iridescent dragonfly, parallax clouds, and mountain sunset) so the game always runs reliably.

- [`index.html`](file:///home/agent/workspace/index.html) – HTML structure, viewport configurations, HUD, video container, and overlays.
- [`style.css`](file:///home/agent/workspace/style.css) – Mobile safe-area constraints, desktop pillarbox layout, and modal styling.
- [`game.js`](file:///home/agent/workspace/game.js) – Core game engine, physics, state machine, and Web Audio synthesizer.
- [`assets/`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/) – Game assets: [`title.mp4`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/title.mp4), [`bird.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/bird.png), [`insect.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/insect.png), [`background.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/background.png), [`cloud.png`](file:///home/agent/workspace/assets/cloud.png).

Tasks:

1. Inspect all three attached PNG images.
2. Copy the original images into the project’s assets folder.
3. Rename them as:
    * bird_fly_1.png
    * bird_fly_2.png
    * bird_fly_3.png
4. Preserve the original PNG transparency (alpha channel). Do not convert them to JPEG.
5. Implement a smooth wing-flapping animation using these three images.
6. Cycle through the images at approximately 8–12 frames per second.
7. Keep the bird’s position, size, and alignment consistent between frames.
8. Use the animation during gameplay on both smartphones and PCs.
9. Preserve all existing gameplay mechanics and other assets.
10. Test the animation in the running game and fix any issues.
